content.text: {"label":"unknown_demand_surge","explanation":"General has run about 30% above forecast all day (2600 vs 2004 calls), steadily at +28-39% each interval. The excess is spread across every call reason (ratios 1.17-1.6) rather than concentrated in one. Nothing in the information explains it. The two open incidents are P4 with no customer impact. The only campaign was a fraud-awareness social post, which would drive payments fraud reports, not broad general demand. General absences (1) are below the usual level (2.2), and handle times are near forecast, so this is not a supply or system problem. Payments is only mildly above forecast (+10%) and holding 97-100% service level.","plan_name":"Sustain general cover after the morning levers expire","rationale":"General service level is currently 92-100%, but only because extra staff were on: agents on phones ran 36-40 against 29-33 planned. Most of the morning levers have now expired: overtime ended 15:30, coaching cancellation 15:00, callback 15:00, and chat deflection ends 16:00. Volume is still about 84 calls per 15 min at roughly 370 s handle time, which needs about 35 busy agents, while only about 37 are on phones. That leaves too little headroom to hold 80% in 20 s. The plan replaces the lost capacity: (1) Renew chat deflection on the two eligible general reasons until close, about 75 chats or Rs 900. (2) Move 4 cross-skilled agents from payments, which has around 43 agents for about 33 Erlangs of work and stays well above 70% with 39. (3) A modest overtime offer of 10 agents, about 4 accepting, roughly Rs 2,900, which fits within the Rs 6,360 left after the morning's estimated Rs 8,640. (4) Cancel any remaining general coaching. (5) Delay late-afternoon general breaks for free borrowed capacity; agents already delayed at 11:00 are skipped automatically.
